question: An if-statement can exist without an else clause.
In Python, you must use parentheses around the condition in an if-statement.
The else clause in an if-statement executes only if the if condition is true.
It is legal to have multiple elif clauses in a single if-statement.
The following code will produce a syntax error: 'if x < 10 print(x)'
If the condition of an if-statement is false, all subsequent elif clauses are also skipped.
You can use logical operators 'and' and 'or' within an if-statement condition in Python.
The statement 'if True: print('Always True!')' will print 'Always True!' exactly once.
In nested if-statements, the inner if will execute even if the outer if fails.
Improper indentation of an if-statement in Python will raise an IndentationError.
